description:
FOUND s438i (Opus 5) as the named residue of #450, whose task text asked for
exactly this check before writing the no-wildcard predicate.

    perl                        PCL
    glob("{a,b}")   -> a, b     (empty)
    glob("x{1,2}y") -> x1y x2y  (empty)

bsd_glob implements csh-style brace expansion BEFORE any filesystem matching,
and the words it produces need not exist -- `{a,b}` yields the literal strings
`a` and `b`.  PCL's p-glob--expand has no brace pass, so the pattern reaches
the directory matcher, matches nothing, and answers empty.

UNCHANGED BY #450, deliberately: that fix returns a pattern with no
METACHARACTER as itself, and `{` is counted as a metacharacter precisely so
`{a,b}` does NOT take that path -- answering the literal `{a,b}` would be
further from perl than the empty result.  `%p-glob--wildcard-p` is the one
place to change when this is implemented.

FIX SHAPE: a brace pass in front of `%p-glob--expand-one`, expanding
innermost-first and cross-producting nested groups, then each result word goes
through the existing pipeline (tilde -> no-metachar literal -> matcher).
Perl's own edge cases to probe first: an UNMATCHED `{` is literal
(`glob("{a")`), a comma-less group is literal (`glob("{a}")` -- probe, csh and
bsd_glob differ here), nesting (`{a,{b,c}}`), and a brace inside a character
class (`[{]`).

BAR: the probe table above plus those edge cases; a row in
Pl/t/punct-array-glob-01.t beside #450's; `cl/` change, so the full sweep is
the gate (invisible to corpus-diff) plus the io/ and op/ companion dirs.
subject: glob does not do csh BRACE EXPANSION: `glob("{a,b}")` is empty where perl gives a, b -- the one row of #450's probe table still diverging
